detail: DHCS states that starting January 1, 2027, some adults (19-64 who get Medi-Cal through the ACA expansion) will need to work, volunteer, go to school, or be in training to keep Medi-Cal; Medi-Cal will send a letter if this applies.

value: MAGI New Adult Group (aid code M1) plus applicable 1115 populations
detail: DHCS implementation materials define the subject population as the MAGI New Adult Group (ACA adult expansion), including adults covered under the state expansion for immigrants.

item: Ways to meet the rule (DHCS member materials)
value: Work and earn at least $580/month; seasonal work averaging $580/month over 6 months; job training 80 hours/month; volunteering or community service 80 hours/month; school at least half-time; or a mix totaling 80 hours or $580
detail: DHCS member-facing list of qualifying options; the DHCS outreach letter to members states income can be from any source.
notes: See flagged items: member page says work at a job and earn at least $580, while the MEDIL outreach letter says income from any source.

value: Outreach letters mailed from late August 2026; member letter states the rules will not go into effect until March 2027
detail: The DHCS outreach letter tells current members the Work and Community Engagement Rule and 6-Month Renewal Rule will not go into effect until March 2027; counties must include the outreach letter with application materials from October 1 through December 31, 2026.
notes: New applicants are subject to the requirement from the January 1, 2027 implementation date; see flagged items for the date framing.

detail: Some members (adults 19-64 in the ACA expansion group) will have eligibility checked twice a year instead of once; missing deadlines can cause loss of coverage.
notes: CMS issued guidance (SMD #26-001, March 2026) on six-month renewals.

value: Chapter 209, Statutes of 2026; signed by Governor Newsom September 14, 2026
detail: Amends Welfare and Institutions Code 14005.69. Requires counties to verify information through available data when possible, maintain coverage during the 30-day response period for enrollees, check whether applicants or beneficiaries qualify for Medi-Cal on another basis before denying or terminating, and resolve conflicting information with the individual before taking adverse action.
notes: Signing recorded on the Governor's site (gov.ca.gov, September 14, 2026).

detail: Medi-Cal will pay fewer past medical bills: adults 19-64 without children get one month of retroactive coverage; everyone else gets two months.

Some adults 19-64 (not pregnant, not on Medicare, making more than $15,560 a year per the DHCS member page) may owe copayments for certain services, capped at 5 percent of household income per year; no copays for emergency care, checkups, pregnancy care, pediatric care, mental health and substance use treatment, or community clinic services.
notes: The $15,560 figure does not match 2025 ($15,650) or 2026 ($15,960) 100% FPL for one person - flagged for review.

value: Up to 233,000 members may lose coverage by June 2027; about 1 million by January 2028; about 1.4 million by June 2028
detail: DHCS stakeholder presentation estimates (February 2026); all numbers are estimates and subject to change.

item: No work requirement in effect today
value: Medi-Cal currently does not require beneficiaries to work to be eligible
detail: The LAO notes Medi-Cal has no work requirement today; DHCS member materials place the work rules under January 2027.

detail: States must send outreach through at least two modalities (mail or electronic notice plus at least one more method); DHCS began a staggered text campaign in February 2026 and mailing outreach notices in late August 2026.

value: CMS initial guidance December 2025; CMS interim final rule June 1, 2026 (effective July 31, 2026)
detail: DHCS tracks both the December 2025 CMS information bulletin and the June 2026 interim final rule (Federal Register June 3, 2026) on its federal impact page.
